GRANDMA’S MID-AUTUMN LANTERNS When Mrs Hoa was a child, her family made paper lanterns for the Mid-Autumn Festival every year. Her father cut thin pieces of bamboo, while her mother prepared coloured paper. (13) ______. The children carried the finished lanterns around the village on the night of the festival. After Mrs Hoa moved to the city, she continued the tradition with her own children. At first, they found the work difficult because they had never used bamboo in this way. (14) ______. After several attempts, each child was able to make a simple star-shaped lantern. As the children grew older, they became busy with their studies. The family began buying plastic lanterns instead, and the paper-lantern tradition gradually stopped. (15) ______. Several years later, Mrs Hoa’s oldest daughter had a child of her own. She asked her mother to show her how to make the lanterns again. (16) ______. Soon, three generations of the family were working together around the same table. The new lanterns were not perfect, but they had a special meaning for the family. Mrs Hoa’s grandchildren now look forward to making them every year. (17) ______.Question 13A. The family usually bought all their lanterns from a shop near the village.B. Her parents kept the bamboo in a locked room until the festival ended.C. Mrs Hoa showed them each step and allowed them to practise slowly.B. The children decided that paper lanterns were no longer worth making.C. The children sold their old schoolbooks to buy more bamboo.B. The family began celebrating a completely different festival.C. Mrs Hoa opened a shop that sold lanterns throughout the year.D. Mrs Hoa worried that her grandchildren might never learn how to make one.Write A, B, C, or D – {#3}Question 16A. The family realised that the festival had already ended several weeks earlier.B. Mrs Hoa brought out her old tools and began explaining the process.C. The children chose to watch television while Mrs Hoa worked alone.D. Her daughter bought several factory-made lanterns for the lesson.Write A, B, C, or D – {#4}Question 17A. They believe plastic lanterns should replace all handmade ones.B. The family now avoids talking about how festivals were celebrated in the past.C. By passing down the skill, the family has brought an old tradition back to life.D. Mrs Hoa’s grandchildren think the lanterns have no connection with their family.Write A, B, C, or D – {#5}
